transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… thank you. I guess what finally made me come in is my eating has been kind of… inconsistent. I don’t know if that sounds serious enough, but some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers or sweets. I just thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

I haven’t really tracked my weight closely, so I don’t want to overstate it. But my appetite has definitely been… kind of all over the place. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’ll end up in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets. I’m not sure if that answers what you mean.
Do you find that you eat more when you're feeling stressed or upset?

I think… maybe sometimes, yes. I don’t want to make it sound like it’s constant, but when I’m stressed or upset, that’s when I’m more likely to end up in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed, eating crackers or something sweet. Other weeks, though, I barely touch dinner, so it kind of swings around. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel guilty after eating?

Sometimes, yes… I mean, not always just because I ate. It’s more like afterward I’ll start thinking I shouldn’t have done that, or I’ll replay other little things too, like buying a tube of pigment that cost too much, or snapping at my spouse. Then it can turn into this whole… “I’ve ruined everything for the household” feeling, which I know probably sounds dramatic. But I can sit with that guilt for hours. Does that make sense?
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour or two?

I don’t know if I’d call it a “large amount,” exactly… maybe not like a binge, if that’s what you mean. But there are nights where, after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll stand in the kitchen and eat crackers or sweets kind of quickly, and then realize I’ve had more than I meant to. It’s not every night—some weeks I barely touch dinner—so it’s been sort of all over the place. Does that answer it okay?
Do you ever try to make up for what you've eaten by doing something to counteract it, like exercising or vomiting?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I might tell myself I’ll “be better tomorrow” or try not to snack as much, but I don’t make myself throw up or exercise to undo it or anything like that. At least, not that I can think of. Is that what you mean?
When you're eating those crackers or sweets at night, do you feel like you can stop whenever you want?

I want to say yes, because it’s not like I feel completely out of control… but honestly, some nights it feels harder to stop than I’d like to admit. I’ll just be standing there after everyone’s gone to bed, having crackers or sweets, and I kind of keep going even after I meant to stop. Other weeks I barely eat dinner, so it’s just been really inconsistent. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
When you're eating at night and you keep going even after you meant to stop, do you feel like you're in control of your eating during those moments?

I guess… not completely, no. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but on those nights when I’m in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s asleep, I’ll keep going even though I already told myself to stop. It’s not like every single night—some weeks I barely touch dinner at all—but the back-and-forth with my eating is kind of what pushed me to come in. Does that make sense?
How often do you have nights where you keep eating even after you meant to stop?

It’s not every night… I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing that constantly. But there are definitely nights like that, especially when everyone’s gone to bed, where I end up in the kitchen with crackers or sweets and keep eating past when I meant to stop.

And then other weeks it’s almost the opposite, like I barely touch dinner. That back-and-forth is really what finally made me think I should come in. Is that helpful?
How many times a month would you say you have nights where you keep eating even after you meant to stop?

I’m not totally sure, honestly—I haven’t been keeping count. I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more that my eating has been really all over the place… some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets and I go past where I meant to stop. That’s the part that made me feel like I should come in.
Do you have these nights where you keep eating even after you meant to stop at least once a week?

I’m not sure I can honestly say it’s at least once every single week. I haven’t been tracking it, and I don’t want to exaggerate. It’s more that my eating has felt really inconsistent—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers or sweets and going past where I meant to stop. That’s really what finally made me think I should come in.
Do you have nights where you feel like you've lost control while eating more often than once a month?

Probably, yes… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but more than once a month sounds right. What finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has been all over the place—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers or sweets and I just keep going longer than I meant to. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you have these episodes of eating more than you meant to, like with the crackers or sweets at night, at least twice a week?

I don’t think I can honestly say twice a week, no… or at least I haven’t been tracking it closely enough to say that. What I do know is my eating has been really all over the place—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers or sweets and I go past what I meant to. I’m sorry if that’s not specific enough.
Do you have episodes where you eat more than you intended, like with the crackers or sweets at night, at least once a week?

I think… probably some weeks, yes, but I’m hesitant to say it’s definitely every week because I haven’t written it down. What pushed me to come in is more that my eating has been really all over the place—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets. I know that’s not a perfect answer… is that okay?
Do you have episodes where you feel like you've lost control while eating at least once a week?

I think so… at least it feels that way some weeks. I don’t want to overstate it, but what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating just feels really all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers and sweets, and it’s like I keep going past what I meant to. Is that what you mean by lost control?
Do you have episodes where you feel like you've lost control while eating at least three times a week?

Three times a week… I’m not sure I can say that. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. What I do know is what I said before—my eating has just been all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets and going past what I meant to. I’m sorry, I know that’s not a clean yes or no.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after these episodes where you feel like you've lost control while eating?

Yes… I mean, I try not to make a big deal of it, but I do feel guilty after. Sometimes it’s not even just the eating, it turns into me replaying everything I did wrong. Like I can spend hours thinking about some small thing—buying an expensive tube of pigment, or snapping at my spouse—and then I feel like I’ve somehow ruined the whole household because of it. That sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, but that’s kind of how it feels.
On average, how many times a week do you have episodes where you eat more than you intended and feel like you've lost control?

I guess on average… maybe once or twice a week? It’s hard to pin down because some weeks I barely eat dinner at all, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers and sweets and I go past what I meant to. I don’t want to exaggerate it, but it has felt kind of all over the place.
Do you often have episodes where you feel like you've lost control while eating?

Often might be a little strong, maybe… but yes, it does happen. That’s part of what finally made me come in—my eating has been really all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers or sweets, and I keep going past where I meant to stop. Does that make sense?
Do you frequently have episodes where you feel like you've lost control while eating?

I think… yes, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It’s not every day. But what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has been all over the place—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’ll stand in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers and sweets, and I feel like I’ve gone past where I meant to stop.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of eating inconsistent amounts, feeling guilty after eating, and experiencing episodes where they feel like they've lost control while eating are more closely aligned with Other eating disorder, specifically a pattern of eating that is characterized by a lack of control and marked distress, but does not meet the full criteria for bulimia nervosa or binge eating disorder.
